help.title: What the columns mean, and what they miss
help.attributed: Attributed: total allocations whose innermost frame inside the traceback belongs to this plugin. It answers "who asked for this memory", including memory the plugin requested through the stdlib or third-party libraries.
help.direct: Direct: the part of Attributed whose innermost frame is the plugin's own code. A large gap means most memory is allocated by libraries the plugin calls.
help.exclusive: Exclusive: walking the reference graph from the plugin instance and its modules, the total size of objects reachable only from this plugin. It answers "what cannot be freed while the plugin stays loaded".
help.shared: Shared: size of objects reachable from more than one plugin. Kept out of Exclusive to avoid double counting.
help.trend: Trend: least-squares slope over recent samples, scaled to one hour. A steadily positive value usually means a leak or a growing cache.
help.limits: Limits: tracemalloc only sees Python-level allocations. C extension buffers (numpy, PIL) and interpreter overhead are invisible, so the plugin totals are much smaller than process RSS. Tracing itself costs roughly 10-30% extra memory and CPU.
help.env: For complete data start AstrBot with PYTHONTRACEMALLOC=12 so tracing is active before any plugin is imported.
help.cost: Cost: a normal refresh only reads a snapshot and is cheap. A deep scan walks the reference graph and can stall for hundreds of milliseconds to a few seconds.
